summary.description: A colourless, odourless gas that is very reactive and highly flammable, used in chemical industry for producing antifreeze, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals
environmental_impact: Long-term low-level exposure causes skin and eye irritation
High concentrations can damage water ecosystems

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Ethylene oxide is a known carcinogen that poses significant health risks to humans. Even low-level, long-term exposure can cause skin and eye irritation, while higher exposures present serious cancer risks, directly threatening human health and wellbeing.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG9_Industry_Innovation_and_Infrastruct: The pollutant is primarily released from chemical industries that use ethylene oxide in manufacturing processes. Managing its emissions requires industrial innovation, improved safety infrastructure, and cleaner production technologies to balance economic needs with environmental protection.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Ethylene oxide is used to produce everyday consumer products like cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and antifreeze. Responsible consumption and production patterns are needed to minimize releases while maintaining the benefits of these essential products through safer manufacturing processes.
